runs.name: Ternium S.A.; Luxembourg, a 20-F filer, NYSE ADSs only, one ADS = 10 ordinary shares; Ternium Brasil bought 2017, Usiminas consolidated 2023; no rename, merger, spin-off or split in the 6-Ks since 2025-03
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$58.99 per ADS, $5.899 per share** (close 2026-10-13 through `tools/sources.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **1,963,076,776**, one class (2,004,743,442 issued on the 20-F cover, `cover_shares.py` the same, less 41,666,666 treasury shares repurchased from Usiminas in 2011; the H1 2026 weighted average the same; Item 16E no purchases in 2025); cap **$11,580M**; net debt **$319M** at 2026-06-30 (after the February 2026 Usiminas purchase), the CSN provision of $599.1M shown beside, not in net debt. Sovereign **5.60%** (US Treasury par curve, 30-year, 2026-10-09; owner earnings in USD, the reporting and main functional currency). Filings read: 20-F FY2025 (`0001342874-26-000020`, Items 3.D, 4, 5, 6.B, 7, 8.A, 16E, notes 5, 25, 32), the 2026 half-year statements (6-K `0001342874-26-000046`), the Q2 2026 release, the dividend revision 6-K of 2026-04-15, the 20-Fs FY2023, FY2020 and FY2017 for the cycle; one figure cross-checked (2025 net sales $15,609M and operating cash $2,313,625 thousand against the filed statements). Not read: the 2026 annual-meeting documents and the analyst-day 6-K of 2026-10-08. `tools/run.py` printed nothing (US-GAAP tags; the filer reports IFRS); the ten-year table was built from the IFRS company facts and checked against the filed cash flow statements. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 20-F's Items 4, 3.D and 5 (the brief's departure for a 20-F filer), stated in the run file: how prices are set, the filer's own statement of its cost position, margins and returns against the named SEC-filing rivals over the span, imports and trade measures in each home market, the parts reported. Competitors: Nucor, ArcelorMittal and Gerdau from their XBRL facts, flagged as not read against their filed statements; the named rivals that do not file flagged in the run file. Balance sheets 2016 to 2026-06-30 read in Step 0: two steps in size by acquisition (Ternium Brasil 2017, Usiminas consolidated 2023), owners' equity $4.4B to $11.9B by 2022 then flat, goodwill small ($662M), net cash 2020 to 2025, about $0.8B of the cash in Argentina and not freely movable. Q1 IN (steel 96% of 2025 sales: Mexico 48%, Brazil through Usiminas 25%, Argentina 16%; a price-taking regional steelmaker readable from ten years of IFRS dollar accounts). **Q2 OUT**: the filer prices "in response to changes in the import prices of foreign steel" and says it may be unable to recover cost increases; foreign producers supply about half of Mexican flat-steel demand, Brazilian flat imports up about 40%, 10% and 30% in 2023 to 2025; a search of the 20-F found no claim of a low-cost position; Usiminas wrote down $405M of deferred tax assets in 2025 citing Chinese imports; 2019 to 2025 pretax margin 12.7% against Nucor 13.9%, Gerdau 11.8%, ArcelorMittal 7.0%, return on equity 12.5% against 23.2%, 15.4% and 7.8%, 7.4% without 2021 and 2.9% over 2023 to 2025, lowest margin of the four in 2024 and second lowest in 2025; the protection mostly government trade measures. The analyst records TOO HARD (NATURE) as the alternative reading (no filing states the cost position; the decade turns on US and Mexican trade policy) and holds OUT under the ordinary-returns rule because the full-cycle returns are known. Q3 to Q12 not reached. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged:** the Superior Court of Justice's reversal of June 2024 ordering indemnification on the 2012 Usiminas tag-along claim (provision $599.1M); 2025 payments of $406M for services and $429.6M for equipment to companies controlled by San Faustin, the controlling shareholder; the 2025 dividend proposal cut from $2.70 to $2.20 per ADS two months after it was announced; Adjusted EBITDA leading the releases. After the stop: capital spending $524M to $2,501M a year over 2021 to 2025 against depreciation of $592M to $788M, about $5.8B over 2023 to 2025 (the Pesqueria downstream lines and a DRI-EAF slab shop due early 2027). COMPUTATION beneath the stop: cycle base 2019 to 2025 trough to trough by operating income (2021 a peak, specific (a)), maintenance-only owner cash all-equity **$1,523M** a year ($921M all-spending); growth 28.9% cut under specific (f) to the business's own sales growth, 9.5%, itself mostly bought; not a serial acquirer; owners' share of value 73.5% at book, a CONVENTION of the run for the minority interests (Usiminas 76.7%, Ternium Argentina 37.4%, Tenigal 49% minority); range **$100.60 to $214.81 per ADS ($10.06 to $21.48 per share)** against $58.99, width 2.12 to 1; fair **$82.28 per ADS all-equity ($8.23 per share)**, **$83.98 equity-only ($8.40)**; beside: $80.04 with the CSN provision deducted, $93.86 at the 2021 to 2025 profit split, $50.56 on the literal window (declining 7.1% a year, specific (b)), $49.27 all-spending. Contamination declared by the analyst: the session's commit subjects showed the CMC run's Q2 OUT (a steel producer, declared as a priming risk); a filtered listing of `Test Runs/` showed the TXN, MATX and TXRH file names, none opened, the self-audit box left unticked for it. Commits a5209c30 to 8a0556fa, four. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for TX or Ternium). Citations: the analyst's check passed; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_check.py` 45 ids, 22 quoted cites, no missing id, no E-id, no slip. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) the commodity paragraph's TOO HARD (NATURE) where no filing states the cost position and the ordinary-returns rule's OUT point different ways, and the text does not say which governs (the CMC run of the same day raised the same split); (2) the all-equity basis does not address minority interests in the operating subsidiaries, a judgment worth about 14% of the figure here; (3) specific (c) does not fit a step acquisition paid mostly before the window (Usiminas consolidated in 2023 for $118.7M of window cash, about $4B of yearly sales credited as growth); (4) specific (a) defines the cycle by owner cash, which here has no clean troughs, so the analyst dated it by operating income; (5) the template does not say whether a Step 0 balance-sheet reading carries a verdict; (6) the brief asked for the annual-meeting documents, which serve Q5 and Q6 and were left unread after the Q2 stop. Could not get: the annual-meeting documents, the analyst-day 6-K, the peers' filed statements, scuttlebutt; whether U.S. Steel and Grupo Simec still file not checked.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: the Americas flat-steel producer (Mexico, Usiminas in Brazil, Argentina), its price set off the import offer in the filer's own words and no filing stating a low-cost position; 2019 to 2025 pretax margin 12.7% against Nucor 13.9%, Gerdau 11.8% and ArcelorMittal 7.0%, return on equity 12.5% against Nucor 23.2%, 2.9% over 2023 to 2025, at or near the bottom of the field in 2024 and 2025, the protection mostly government trade measures; the analyst records TOO HARD (NATURE) as the alternative reading. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the Usiminas tag-along ruling (provision $599.1M), $835.6M of 2025 payments to companies of the controlling shareholder, the 2025 dividend proposal cut two months after announcement. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: range $100.60 to $214.81 per ADS against $58.99, fair $82.28 per ADS all-equity, $83.98 equity-only, the minorities' share a CONVENTION of the run.
